subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging IGCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the Cambridge spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: What is the denary (base-10) value of the 8-bit binary number 01101011?
questions.explain: Column values 64+32+8+2+1 = 107. The set bits are in the 64, 32, 8, 2 and 1 columns.

questions.q: Which 8-bit binary number represents the denary value 200?
questions.explain: 200 = 128 + 64 + 8, so the 128, 64 and 8 columns are set: 11001000.

questions.q: What is the hexadecimal equivalent of the binary number 10111110?
options: DE
AF
EB
BE
questions.explain: Split into nibbles: 1011 = B and 1110 = E, giving BE.

questions.q: What is the denary value of the hexadecimal number 2F?
Two 8-bit binary numbers are added: 11001101 + 01000110. What problem occurs and what is the result within 8 bits?
options: Overflow occurs; the true answer needs 9 bits and the 8-bit result 00010011 is incorrect
Underflow occurs; result is 10001011
No overflow; result is 00010011
No overflow; result is 100010011
questions.explain: 205 + 70 = 275, which exceeds 255 (the max for 8 bits). A carry out of the most significant bit causes overflow, so the retained 8-bit result 00010011 (19) is wrong.

questions.q: In an 8-bit unsigned system, overflow occurs when:
options: a number is shifted left
the sum is greater than 255 and cannot fit in 8 bits
the result is an even number
two negative numbers are added
questions.explain: An 8-bit unsigned register holds 0-255. Overflow happens when a calculation produces a value larger than 255, generating a carry out of the most significant bit.

questions.q: The 8-bit number 00010110 undergoes a logical shift LEFT of 2 places. What is the result?
questions.explain: Shifting left 2 places moves every bit two columns left, filling the right with zeros: 01011000. This multiplies the value by 4 (22 becomes 88).

questions.q: What is the effect of a logical shift RIGHT by 1 place on an unsigned binary number?
options: It reverses the bit order
It divides the value by 2 (integer division), and bits shifted out are lost
It converts it to two's complement
It multiplies the value by 2
questions.explain: A logical right shift by 1 divides by 2. Zeros fill from the left and any bits shifted off the right end are discarded.

questions.q: What is the denary value of the 8-bit two's complement number 11110000?
questions.explain: The leading 1 means it is negative. Invert (00001111) and add 1 (00010000 = 16), so the value is -16.

questions.q: Which 8-bit two's complement number represents -5?
Which statement best describes the advantage of Unicode over ASCII?
options: Unicode uses fewer bits per character so files are smaller
Unicode compresses data automatically
Unicode stores images as well as text
Unicode can represent characters from many more languages and symbols than ASCII
questions.explain: ASCII (typically 7 or 8 bits) covers a limited English character set. Unicode uses more bits per character, allowing it to represent characters from most of the world's writing systems.

questions.q: In ASCII the character 'A' has the denary code 65. What is the denary ASCII code for the character 'D'?
questions.explain: ASCII codes for uppercase letters are consecutive: A=65, B=66, C=67, D=68.

questions.q: What does 'colour depth' of an image describe?
options: The number of pixels across the width of the image
The physical size of the screen
The compression ratio of the image file
The number of bits used to represent the colour of each pixel
questions.explain: Colour depth is the number of bits per pixel. More bits means more possible colours (e.g. 8 bits per pixel = 256 colours).

questions.q: An image is 100 pixels wide by 50 pixels high with a colour depth of 8 bits per pixel. What is its approximate file size in bytes (ignoring headers)?
options: 5 000 bits
5 000 bytes
40 000 bytes
50 000 bytes
questions.explain: Total bits = 100 x 50 x 8 = 40 000 bits. Divide by 8 to get bytes: 5 000 bytes.

questions.q: What does the 'sampling resolution' of a digital sound recording refer to?
options: The length of the recording in seconds
How many samples are taken each second
The number of bits used to store each sample
The loudness of the sound
questions.explain: Sampling resolution (bit depth) is the number of bits used for each sample. Higher resolution gives a more accurate representation of the amplitude. Sampling rate is the separate measure of samples per second.

questions.q: Increasing the sampling rate of a sound recording will generally:
options: have no effect on quality or size
convert the file to lossy format automatically
increase the accuracy of the recording and increase the file size
reduce the file size and reduce accuracy
questions.explain: A higher sampling rate takes more samples per second, giving a more accurate reproduction of the original sound but producing a larger file.

questions.q: How many bits are there in one nibble?
questions.explain: A nibble is 4 bits (half a byte). A byte is 8 bits.

questions.q: Using the IEC units in the Cambridge syllabus, how many bytes are in one kibibyte (1 KiB)?
options: 1024 bits
1000 bytes
1024 bytes
8 bytes
questions.explain: The Cambridge 0478 syllabus uses IEC binary units where 1 kibibyte (KiB) = 1024 bytes, 1 mebibyte (MiB) = 1024 KiB, and so on.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes lossy from lossless compression?
options: Lossless can only be used on sound files
Lossy keeps all original data; lossless permanently removes data
Both permanently remove data equally
Lossy permanently removes some data to reduce size; lossless reduces size with no permanent loss of data
questions.explain: Lossy compression permanently discards data (e.g. detail the ear/eye may not notice). Lossless compression reduces file size so the original data can be perfectly reconstructed.

questions.q: Run length encoding (RLE) is most effective on data that contains:
options: only text in English
long runs of repeated identical values
completely random values with no repeats
encrypted data
questions.explain: RLE replaces runs of repeated values with a single value plus a count, so it works best when there are long sequences of identical data (e.g. large blocks of one colour in an image).
